inputs.name: shortfall
inputs.cite: parameters shortfall.mittens3_full, shortfall.mittens3_snv_only; quotes-day.md row 14; M-901.json

day.reading: each fixation takes a fixed LTEE time, so the required time is the divergence time times the shortfall: orders of magnitude beyond the age of the Universe
day.holds: 6.3e6 x 1.075e6 = 6.7725e12 y = 490.8 universe-ages (2.69 orders); even Day's SNV-only 91,600 gives 41.8 universe-ages; any shortfall above 2,190 exceeds one age

critic.reading: the arithmetic holds only if the shortfall is a time multiplier at a fixed rate; Keen gives no equation and endorses The Frozen Gene, not the MITTENS papers
critic.holds: with a validated scaling and SNV-only counts the multiplier falls to about 10-100, i.e. 6.3e7-6.3e8 y, 0.005-0.046 universe-ages; the 205M counts bp of structural variants

notes: Keen's sentence is checkable only under the claim file's reading (T_required = T_div x shortfall at a fixed per-fixation rate); the preface has no equation and its subject is truncated in the extracted quote. Under that reading it holds at Day's figures (490.8 ages; 100.4 at the older 220,000x). The question is the shortfall, not this multiplication: the break-even is 2,190, so the critics' 10-100 falls below one age and Day's SNV-only 91,600 does not. Whether the shortfall is 1e6, 9e4 or 1e1-1e2 is A, A3x and A5's external question, not settled here.
